deferred.reason: Life-annuity valuation multiplies discount factors by survival probabilities, which is probabilistic estimation outside the assignment boundary (textbook identities and closed deterministic forms only). Continuation priority: keep excluded unless the domain expands to mortality-contingent forms.

deferred.reason: Variable and equity-indexed annuities link payments to market-index performance, which is probabilistic and market-forecasting outside the deterministic boundary. Fixed-rate riders would need their own fee-bearing sources.

queries: What accumulates from $100 end-of-period deposits over 4 periods at 12 percent?
What present value corresponds to 32 beginning-of-quarter payments of $9435.71 at 1.25 percent per quarter?

handoff.review_notes: Arithmetic validated with the kit validator; source fidelity reviewed against the fetched UMD tutorial text and the Annuity article text. Not performed: visual PDF checks (no PDFs used), institutional-textbook confirmation of the due-factor notation beyond the two inspected sources, independent measurement beyond published examples and alternate-route derivations. The annuity-due records are mathematically distinct from uniform-present-value@source-3 by the beginning-of-period timing factor, per the assignment allowance.
handoff.summary: Batch b02 extends the time-value family down the annuity queue: ordinary-annuity accumulation, beginning-of-period (due) present and future values with the source-stated (1+i) timing shift, and the arithmetic-gradient annual equivalent. Each record carries one published oracle plus a boundary or alternate-route check.

assumptions: Source assumption: equal end-of-period deposits with the first one full period after time 0 accumulating at fixed per-period rate i (UMD end-of-year convention).
Application profile: accumulation of a savings or sinking-fund stream with no withdrawals; A and i fixed over the horizon.
All amounts on one price basis.

gaps: Reuses b01 proposed meanings periodic_payment, periodic_rate, period_count, future_value; no current-runtime projection attempted.
The sinking-fund direction (solving A from F) is recorded as an inverse, not a separate model.

models.inverse_notes: A=F*i/((1+i)**n-1) needs i>0 and n>=1; checked against the UMD sinking-fund example 1000*0.12/(1.12**4-1)=209.235 versus the published 209.2 (rounding). Substitution check at n=1: F=A exactly (single end-of-period deposit accumulates nothing). The i-to-0 limit branch F=A*n is a different expression, never a guard relaxation.
limitations: Zero-rate accumulation (i=0) is excluded by guard; its limit branch F=A*n is a separate expression.
Beginning-of-period deposits need the annuity-due record, not this expression.
Solving for the rate or term needs iteration or a logarithm, unsupported by the scalar grammar.

references.method: Source prints F=477.9 for A=100, i=12%, n=4; recomputation gives 477.933, so tolerance covers the $0.1 rounding.

references.method: Boundary identity: one end-of-period deposit accumulates to itself; evaluates the closed form at n=1.

rejection_cases.reason: Zero rate makes the divisor zero and needs the separate limit branch F=A*n; excluded by i>0.

relationship.translation_notes: Transcribed verbatim into scalar syntax. Dimensional check: currency times a dimensionless accumulation factor stays currency. Guards i>0 and n>=1 jointly keep the divisor i and the factor nonzero and positive. Reference exponents 4 and 1 are within the tooling cap.

assumptions: Source assumption: cash flows of 0 at year 1, G at year 2, 2G at year 3, up to (n-1)G at year n, discounted at fixed rate i under the end-of-year convention.
Application profile: maintenance or operating costs rising by a constant arithmetic amount per period; gradient and rate fixed.
All amounts on one price basis.

gaps: Needs new quantity meaning gradient_amount (periodic_payment, periodic_rate, period_count reuse b01 proposals); no current-runtime projection attempted.
The present-value-of-gradient direction is recorded as an inverse, not a separate model.

models.inverse_notes: G=A/(1/i-n/((1+i)**n-1)) needs i>0, n>1; at n=1 the factor is 0 so any G maps to A=0 and the inverse is underdetermined (a single zero-first-period stream carries no gradient information). Checked: 967.83/(1/0.08-10/(1.08**10-1))=250.0. The i-to-0 limit branch A=G*(n-1)/2 is a separate expression, untested here.
limitations: Zero-rate case (i=0) is excluded by guard; its limit branch A=G*(n-1)/2 is a separate expression.
Geometric (percentage-growth) gradients need a distinct growing-annuity record with its own source, not this arithmetic form.
Decreasing series are admitted by the unsigned math but the worked scope is rising costs; sign discipline belongs to the application.
